SELECTED_INDEX: 1  
CONFIDENCE: 0.38  
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows the characteristic strong para-disubstituted benzene ring breathing doublet at 824–853 cm⁻¹, indicating a 1,4-disubstituted phenyl.  A pronounced band at 640 cm⁻¹ matches the aryl C–Cl stretch region (rules GFQ-041 / GFQ-046), so the para partner must be chlorine.  Aliphatic C–H stretches (2921 cm⁻¹) and CH₂/CH₃ deformations (1449 cm⁻¹) are present, while no strong OH stretch is required in Raman.  Among the candidates only molecule 1 (HO-CH₂–C₆H₄–Cl, para-chlorobenzyl alcohol) possesses a para Cl–phenyl along with one benzylic CH₂ group, matching the full pattern of peaks; other Cl-containing candidates give meta substitution or additional side-chain features.  Hence candidate 1 best fits the experimental Raman data.
